author: B Codex critical mechanism and conservation reasoning; hand derivation only
question: With actual owned prepare results, does all-partial long-source admission add complete-copy ACK/cost capability over one-full-sponsor ordinary streaming?

decision.result: Stop the current resident-child performance trial. A concrete future-blind one-full-sponsor controller matches or beats the three chosen continuations at identical transaction and retained-record budgets.
decision.retained_positive_action: The frontier contract permits starting one source envelope before any recipient owns full WRITE coverage. This is a distinct admission action against a controller that requires a full sponsor, but early payload availability alone does not establish complete-copy performance benefit or independent novelty.
decision.not_claimed: No optimality over all streaming policies, no impossibility for redesigned all-partial policies, no current-DUT/FPGA timing result, and no independent-innovation claim from these selected phase examples.
decision.next: Root is pursuing a different, explicitly specified speculative-share-before-READ-validation action. Do not extend this chosen service window into another matrix or RTL experiment.

actual_source_boundary.evidence_owner: Root directly read the critical source; this seat did not repeat the repository reading.
actual_source_boundary.default: Behavioral shared DDR serves FIFO-head R through that burst's RLAST; each accepted AR has ptw_latency, default 31, with countdown only at the head. WREADY defaults to 1.
actual_source_boundary.optional: Overlap plus round-robin beats/DS priority can serve PTE between payload beats; an already held R VALID is not switched. Optional memory backpressure accepts W in 3/4 cycles, not the every-two-cycle environment below.
actual_source_boundary.hardware_limit: The default first-beat 31 is explicitly not MIG matched. It is not a measured FPGA AR cost.
actual_source_boundary.prepare_limit: The existing PREP fixture uses a static Normal-memory validity/cache-PA prototype. A production access_ok/owned-result route is absent.
actual_source_boundary.coupling_limit: Production RAW_COUPLING_AVAIL is 0. The ordinary first-R release used below is a specified implementable adapter action, not a currently enabled or executed production feature.
actual_source_boundary.scope: H=1/3/4, source-first-beat=1, and W period 2 below are chosen legal hand environments. They are not the current test knobs, an actual run, or MIG measurements.

common_contract.cohort: Frozen A and B, immutable ordered physical source N=7 words, each independently owns READ authorization for the entire source and compatible PA/attributes.
common_contract.destination: Each initially owns a continuous WRITE prefix C=6 words; its final one word lies on the next 4 KiB destination page and initially lacks WRITE authorization. Stable Normal mappings, no MMIO, no overlap/alias, no remap/revocation in this witness.
common_contract.payload_budget: Q_A=Q_B=3 actual exclusive payload slots, six total. No shared skid or hidden spill is counted twice. A source word is consumed only after both frozen recipients can really accept it.
common_contract.permission_budget: Three WRITE records: current prefix A, current prefix B, and one global owned result slot. Two common READ records are also charged. No control is granted a free second tail record.
common_contract.real_acquisition: Each tail result actually handshakes with access_ok, PA, attributes, job/cookie and usable grant ownership into the global result slot. It becomes usable in the next slot. READY=0 on a native VALID is not permission acquisition and its PA is not read through an imaginary trusted route.
common_contract.record_lifetime: A prefix record stays valid through its last real physical B. Once that B retires, a tail grant can migrate from the global slot to the vacated per-flow slot. Global capture plus migration costs are charged to both controls. The common trusted lookup may use an already usable global grant for AW while the record migrates; it does not require a second validation or a new PTE. The ownership cookie survives migration until the tail's real B.
common_contract.capture_ports: The one-slot owned-result register permits an ordinary simultaneous consume/replace when the preceding result migrates to an already vacant private slot. Both controls have the same path and ports. A control that cannot do this must account for the additional acquisition gap for both, rather than keep the following times unchanged.
common_contract.write_interface: The same per-flow adapter is upstream of the W-owner mux. It virtualizes physical children while keeping original logical AW/byte cursor/completion pending. It can issue an immutable child AW from actual resident/reserved source data. Physical true WLAST releases a child owner; original logical completion waits for every child's real B. One physical child per flow is active at once, with descriptor reuse only after its B.
common_contract.immutability: No offered AW or W is withdrawn or modified. No MIG-selected/held R is bypassed. Per-ID order, byte/W obligations, own grants and all original ACKs remain intact.
common_contract.source_service: One source AR occupies the ordered R service until its RLAST; tail PTE service is behind it. Each queued cold tail single-leaf read occupies the head service for H consecutive slots, with its one true PTE R and acquisition at the terminal slot and usable lease one slot later. H is head-service time, not H accepted PTE data beats or H different page-table requests. Ready successive leaf reads incur no additional issue gap in this chosen contract. No pre-entry prefetch, native hit or previously acquired tail result is available in these cold witnesses.
common_contract.w_service: W acceptance is available only at absolute even slots 4,6,8,... . An owning burst cannot interleave W with another owner. A real source R accepted at t supplies true W no earlier than t+1; AW accepted at t supplies W no earlier than t+1. Physical B is WLAST+1.
common_contract.first_r_release: After source AR is already accepted, the adapter may commit its first 3-word WRITE child concurrently with the actual first source-R handshake, with all three recipient-private source credits already reserved. Thus its first true W can occur at t_first_R+1. This is a same-cycle first-R qualification, not a prediction of future payload or a new source request.
common_contract.initial_cost: At the common entry the two READ and two prefix-WRITE preparations were already actually acquired; their costs and records are common prehistory. Each complete job still incurs two actual cold tail-WRITE preparations. Total own preparation acquisitions are six for either policy.

strong_ordinary_controller.policy: Prepare A's tail first into the owned global slot; after this actual lease is usable, issue the single source AR7. Use per-flow physical WRITE lengths 3,3,1. Release the first child on actual first R, with the first quantum's private credits reserved. For the second child, commit when A has two true source words and B's actual last W of its first child releases the one private slot needed for the remaining shared source word. Reserve that free slot, then offer the AW in the next slot; do not wait for all three A words to become resident. After RLAST, obtain only B's still-missing tail permission. Complete all true writes and real B responses.
strong_ordinary_controller.why_second_aw_is_legal: For H=3, source words 4/5/6 arrive 13/15/17. B's first child really consumes its third W at 16. At the next slot A has two true words and each recipient has the last source credit reserved; AW17 is immutable, source word 6 accepts at 17, and its data is usable at 18. A's next true W can start at 18. No further READ, PTE or future peer write is needed to retire that 3-word child.
strong_ordinary_controller.information: Only acquired permission, real R/W handshakes, actual private credit, fixed page boundaries, child completion and observed first R. The rule does not know a future source gap, future H outcome or a later grant.
strong_ordinary_controller.no_extra_state: The same child descriptor, private credit reservation and owned permission/cookie slots available to the candidate. It does not add a virtual lane, payload buffer, source replay, second tail record, NULL conversion or new translation work.
strong_ordinary_controller.full_sponsor_scope: Only A is made fully WRITE-ready before source issue. B's already authorized prefix drains and its single unprepared tail word fits its actual Q3. The controller does not require all recipients to be fully prepared and does not implement a maximal all-partial source-end search.

symbolic_schedule.G: G(t) is the least even W-service slot at least t; first eligible W slot is 4.

ordinary.cold_sponsor: Service slots 0..H-1; acquire H-1, usable H; source AR H; first three R H+1,H+2,H+3.
ordinary.w0: w0 = G(max(4,H+2)), using actual-first-R AW qualification.
ordinary.second_source_quantum: R4/R5/R6 at w0+7,w0+9,w0+11; B's real first-child WLAST at w0+10 creates the last reserved source credit; A second AW at w0+11.
ordinary.remaining_ptw: B service w0+20 .. w0+H+19, acquire at its final slot, usable w0+H+20.
ordinary.A_tail_W_ACK: A_W=w0+24; A_ACK=w0+25. A tail grant is already genuinely owned, not re-read from an unaccepted response.
ordinary.B_tail_W_ACK: B_W=G(max(w0+26,w0+H+21)); B_ACK=B_W+1. This includes B prefix's real B, native result usability and A's tail W owner.

candidate_fixed_resident_C3.startup: Source AR -1, source R1/R2/R3 at 0/1/2; full-resident prefix children AW A3/B4.
candidate_fixed_resident_C3.tail_ptw: A service26..H+25, usableH+26; B serviceH+26..2H+25, usable2H+26. Both acquire actual owned results.

symbolic_schedule.bounded_comparison: For this fixed resident-C3 candidate and the specified service/adapter contract, the ordinary formulas give both ACKs no later for integer H>=1. For H>=5, A is equal or 2 earlier depending parity and ordinary B is 4 earlier; H1..4 are explicitly checked below. This is not a theorem about all all-partial policies or different W/AR environments.

complete_finite_witnesses.preserved_conservative_match: The previously supplied ordinary policy can retain the full-resident second child, giving source_R7=25 and ACK31/33 at identical costs. That conservative countercontrol already refutes unique benefit. The stronger credit-first policy above is also future blind.

complete_finite_witnesses.corrected_original_prediction: A33/B35 and the supposed sum-ACK>=68 sponsor lower bound applied only if the second child waits for full residency until AW18. Actual live credit allows AW17/W18, so that lower bound is false for the permitted ordinary streaming class. Do not keep candidate31/35 as a positive complete-cost separation.

complete_finite_witnesses.first_r_detail: AW5 is qualified by the actual source R1 handshake at5, using already reserved private credit. Its first real W6 uses the data accepted at5. If the available adapter necessarily adds another AW issue cycle, this H4 timing changes; that adapter restriction must apply identically and is an interface cost rather than a general streaming impossibility.

whole_job_cost_ledger.per_job_completion: Both complete all seven true writes and receive all three physical B responses. Their original logical ACK is exactly the final listed B, not physical source RLAST or an early partial child response.
whole_job_cost_ledger.migration_occupancy: Ordinary A retains its owned tail in the global slot until its second prefix B, then migrates to vacant A private storage before B's tail result arrives. Candidate A is acquired only after that prefix B and uses the same capture/migration path; B may hold the global owned result until its old prefix B. The true old-region grant is never overwritten before its B.
whole_job_cost_ledger.unknown_hardware_costs: Trusted result lookup, same-cycle first-R qualification, owned-record capture/transfer, metadata muxing, issue timing and synthesis cost have not been implemented/measured. These hand slots do not assign a measured energy or latency to them.

preserved_failed_claims.resident_only_H1: If every ordinary child waits for all three words before offering AW, sponsor ACK33/35 versus candidate31/33 is a valid restricted comparison. It cannot support a claim against ordinary streaming because actual first-R release already gives a same-cost match, and live credit gives29/31.
preserved_failed_claims.H3_positive: The initial proposed sponsor ACK33/35 lower bound incorrectly forced its second child to wait for complete residency. That would retain a chosen-control point, not prove an online capability boundary. It is explicitly withdrawn here, with the complete legal31/33 countercontrol preserved.
preserved_failed_claims.old_artifacts: No stage85 or earlier design artifact was rewritten. This stage86 card records the strengthened countercontrol and correction; it is not a silent change to earlier tables.

conservation_and_frontier_scope.why_total_R_work_does_not_decide_ACK: Moving A's one tail walk before the source does not remove its work. It can be offset by beginning WRITE with only the actual first word and by reserving a later real free credit before the third word arrives. Native B's tail walk is then the sole critical post-RLAST translation. Conversely a different service/issue contract can change overlap. Equal total work alone implies neither universal equivalence nor universal separation.
conservation_and_frontier_scope.prefetch_and_hits: An actual prior native hit or prefetch result may reduce or remove sponsor startup delay, but must have really acquired permission/ownership and occupied a counted slot. Earlier cold service cannot be credited without the earlier request and causal service opportunity. A TL response held READY0 is not a free leased record and holding a real single TL can prevent another cold walk.
conservation_and_frontier_scope.what_positive_capability_remains: Within the safe all-partial admission contract, first physical payload may be available at0 while a cold one-full-sponsor rule must wait untilH+1. If an independently justified consumer requirement or newly designed policy turns this earlier action into a complete same-budget improvement, that specific difference can be a contribution. The fixed resident-C3 complete-ACK witnesses here do not do so.
conservation_and_frontier_scope.what_this_does_not_eliminate: All-partial admission safety, resource feasibility without any full sponsor, a redesigned all-partial streaming scheduler, or another real interface/service contract. Those are different claims and must have their own one decisive comparison, not inherit this refuted performance point.
conservation_and_frontier_scope.innovation_statement: Because the concrete ordinary controller reproduces or improves every claimed complete-cost point in this bounded trial, these points cannot be used as an independent performance contribution. If a different new action yields a legal same-budget capability or complete-cost advantage not reproduced by the named control and exact primary neighbors, that narrower result can support innovation; it requires separate evidence.
